studies.title: TRACER STUDY OF GRADUATES UNIVERSITIES IN SRI LANKA
studies.subtitle: (Sponsored by the UNESCO Participation Programme 2016/2017)
studies.cohort: State universities: graduated 2014 and 2015 (about 3 and 2 years before the survey). Non-state (SLIIT, APIIT): graduated 2015.
studies.scope: Sample survey (not a census). 14 conventional state universities under the UGC (Open University excluded); Medicine, Dental Surgery, Veterinary Medicine and Indigenous Medicine graduates excluded. Supplementary non-state sample from two institutions (SLIIT, APIIT).
studies.definitionOfEmployed: No formal definition is printed. Status is as reported 'at the time of the survey'; respondents are classified as 'Employed', 'Engaged as a volunteer' or 'Not employed' (Figure 7, p.12). Employed includes part-time: 'Graduates who were employed at the time of survey were classified into two categories: full time employed and part-time employed.' and part-time = 'less than 40 hours a week' (Section 3.4.1, p.35).

definitionQuotes.quote: Employed Engaged as a volunteer Not employed
Graduates who were employed at the time of survey were classified into two categories: full time employed and part-time employed.
89.7% were engaged in full-time employment while 10.3% were engaged in part-time employment (less than 40 hours a week).

studies.responseRate: 25% (1,265 of a potential sample of 5,000; population 30,270). Non-state: 234 of 251 (94 percent).

responseRateQuotes.quote: Of the 5,000 graduates selected from the state sector, the potential sample, only 1,265 (25%) responded to the survey.
A potential sample of 5,000 graduates was selected from the 30,2703 students who graduated in the years 2014 and 2015 from the 14 conventional universities under the purview of the UGC.
responseRateQuotes.note: '30,2703' is '30,270' followed by footnote marker 3 in the PDF text.

responseRateQuotes.quote: A high response rate of 94 percent was achieved in this phase of the survey.
Out of 251 non–state graduates in the sample, 234 graduates responded to the survey.

overall.quote: Out of the 1,265 graduates traced from state universities, 65.5% were employed, 32.2% were unemployed and 2.4% were engaged as volunteers.
In the non-state sector, 66% was employed and 34% was not employed.

timeToJob.quote: Altogether, 43.3% were employed before releasing the final results, 24.4% were employed within six months of receiving the results, and a 16.2% have found a job within the 7 to 12 months of receiving the results. However, there are about 5.6% who have spent more than 2 years to find a job.

timeToJob.group: By stream: found job after final results
timeToJob.quote: The majority of the graduates in the streams of Education (100%), Performing Arts (92.3%), Agriculture (75.4%) and Arts (70.5%) who were employed at the time of survey had found their jobs “after releasing the final results”.
a higher percentage of graduates of Computer Science/IT, Engineering, Architecture and Management have found their first job faster than their counterparts in other streams.

A high percentage of the Performing Arts graduates (23.1%) have taken more than two years to find a job after graduation. Further, among Arts graduates, 12.1% waited for more than 2 years to find a job after graduation.

sectorOfEmployment.quote: 46.2% of which the employment opportunities for graduates are created by the private sector. Teaching positions in the public sector have created the second largest source of employment for graduates (21%).

sectorOfEmployment.quote: On the other hand, all Education graduates (100%) were employed as public sector teachers. Further, a higher percentage of graduates in the fields of Performing Arts (76.9%), Agriculture (36.8%) and Arts (32.9%) were also employed as teachers in public schools.

partTime.quote: part-time employment is comparatively high in the fields of Performing Arts (30.8%), Computer Science/IT (25%) and Education (15.6%) compared to other fields of studies.

notes: Data is old: survey fielded August/September 2017 for 2014-2015 graduates; it is still the most recent national UGC tracer study (ugc.ac.lk/downloads/statistics/webTracer/ holds only a 2018 folder, checked 2026-10-15).

Low and uneven response: 25% overall; by stream from 38.4% (Education) and 35.2% (Arts) down to 7.0% (Comp. Sc./IT) (Figure 1, p.7). The report itself says 'Strangely, the response rate in Architecture and Computer Science/IT fields was low compared to others.' (p.16). The 100% figures for Architecture and Comp. Sc./IT rest on very few respondents and should not be shown without that caveat.

Medicine, Dental Surgery, Veterinary Medicine and Indigenous Medicine were NOT surveyed, 'due to the reason that these graduates are fully absorbed by the state sector for employment' (p.4). The report gives no employment figure for them.

Education stream 100% reflects state absorption into teaching in that period ('fully absorbed into the teaching profession by the Ministry of Education and Provincial Ministries of Education', p.16); the 2023 MoHE compilation reports Education at 32.0%, so this is not stable over time.
Employment measured 2 to 3 years after graduation and includes part-time work (<40 h/week, 10.3% of employed). 'Engaged as a volunteer' (2.4%) is counted separately, not as employed.
Underemployment: 'approximately one in every ten employed graduates of the sample was underemployed' (p.ix).
Small internal inconsistency: text on p.15 gives Sinhala-medium employment as 46.5% while Figure 12's label reads 46.9%. Not used per field.
Page numbers are the printed page numbers (printed p.1 = PDF page 15; Roman-numbered front matter before that).
Non-state sample covers only two institutions (SLIIT, APIIT) and four streams; 'only two non-state institutions agreed to share their information' (p.12).

studies.title: Progress Report 2024 (Higher Education) - Section 4.3 Employability of Graduates
studies.publisher: Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education | Higher Education
studies.cohort: Not stated. The report says the figures are 'for the year 2023'; graduating batch, time since graduation and survey timing are not printed.
studies.scope: Compilation of graduate employability surveys run by individual universities (not one national survey). Sources named: University of Colombo, University of Moratuwa, University of Sri Jayewardenepura, University of Jaffna, University of Ruhuna, Eastern University, South Eastern University, Wayamba University, Open University. Peradeniya, Kelaniya, Rajarata, Sabaragamuwa, Uva Wellassa, UVPA and others are not in the source list.
studies.definitionNote: No definition of 'employed'/'employability' is printed; the text uses 'employability rate' and 'employment rate' interchangeably for the same figures.
studies.responseRateNote: No sample size or response rate is printed.

overall.quote: according to the results of surveys conducted by several universities for the year 2023, the overall graduate employability rate in 2023 is 69.1%.

byField.fieldNote: University of Colombo only: 'According to the University of Colombo, the employability rate of medical graduates is 76.2%.'

byField.field: Mass Media and Performing Arts ( Sri Palee Campus)
byField.quote: Mass Media and Performing Arts ( Sri Palee Campus) 35.5

byUniversity.quote: In 2023, the University of Moratuwa reported an employability rate of 85.5%, the Open University reported an employability rate of 93.8%, the Wayamba University reported an employment rate of 72.3%, the University of Sri Jayewardenepura reported an employability rate of 71.4%, the South Eastern University reported an employability rate of 67.5%, the University of Colombo reported an employment rate of 66.8%, and the Universities of Ruhuna, Jaffna, and Eastern reported an employability rate of 58.1%, 53.5%, and 52.8% respectively.

notes: Most recent official per-field figures found, but they are a ministry compilation of separate university surveys: methods, timing after graduation, definitions and response rates are not stated and probably differ by university.
Not national: only 9 institutions listed as sources (including the Open University, whose students are often already employed, 93.8%). Large universities such as Peradeniya and Kelaniya are absent.

A field's figure may come from one or two universities (e.g. Medicine = University of Colombo only; Quantity Surveying, Facilities Management, Town and Country Planning are Moratuwa-type programmes). Sample sizes per field are not printed, so small-n fields cannot be identified.
Overall rate printed twice with different values: 69.1% (text and Figure 4.2 'All', p.20) vs 'Average 69.2' (Table 4.5, p.21).

Figure 4.2's source caption lists 'North Western University' while Table 4.5's lists 'Wayamba University' (Wayamba University of Sri Lanka is in the North Western Province); the text says 'Wayamba University'.

Text on p.21 says the subject data is 'based on calculations from the University of Colombo, University of Sri Jayewardenepura, University of Jaffna, University of Ruhuna, Eastern University, South Eastern University, Wayamba University, and the Open University' (Moratuwa not in that sentence, though it is in the table's source caption).
No public vs private split and no time-to-job figures are given.
Page numbers are printed page numbers (printed p.20 = PDF page 29; p.21 = PDF page 30).

studies.title: GRADUATE EMPLOYABILITY 2020 University of Kelaniya
studies.publisher: University Statistics & Data Monitoring Unit, University of Kelaniya
studies.cohort: Main cohort graduating in 2020 (2017/18 academic year); repeat candidates and Medicine excluded.
studies.scope: ONE university only (University of Kelaniya), four faculties. Included as an example of a university's own published tracer survey, not national data.
studies.definitionOfEmployed: Graduate employment rate of the University of Kelaniya is calculated based on the sample proportion who are employed by the time of survey which is within the first 10 months of the graduation (results valid date) of each year. Accordingly, the sample employment rate is the ratio of employed graduates to which the total number of responses.
studies.responseRate: 79% (1755 responses of 2,226 accessible population, Table 1-3, p.11); text also says 'the overall response rate was 78%'.

responseRateQuotes.quote: Accordingly, the overall response rate was 78%.

labourForce.title: Sri Lanka Labour Force Survey Annual Report - 2025
labourForce.publisher: Department of Census and Statistics, Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development
labourForce.sample: The total sample size for the annual survey results for 2025 report were based on 25,000 housing units which were selected using a known probability sampling technique.
labourForce.definitionOfEmployed: Employed: Persons, who during the reference period, worked as paid employees, employers, own account workers, or unpaid family workers are said to be employed. This includes persons with a job but not at work during the reference period.
labourForce.definitionOfUnemployed: Unemployed: Persons who are seeking and available for work, but had no employment during the reference period.
labourForce.referencePeriodNote: Reference period is the week before the survey week (Explanatory notes, p.84). Ages 15 and over.

notFound: No UGC tracer / graduate employment study newer than the 2018 report (survey 2017). The ugc.ac.lk/downloads/statistics/webTracer/ directory lists only a '2018/' folder (checked 2026-10-15). UGC 'Sri Lanka University Statistics' yearbooks (2020-2024) carry graduate output counts, not employment.
No UGC 'Graduate Employment Census' was found on ugc.ac.lk.

MoHE 'Employability Study of University Graduands of Sri Lanka (2012)' is listed on mohe.gov.lk, but its file (/images/pdf/Overall_FINAL_report_2012.pdf) returned HTTP 404 on both www.mohe.gov.lk and mohe.gov.lk (2026-10-15).
MoHE 'Annual Performance Report 2025' (HE_Annual_Report_2025_English.pdf) contains no graduate employability figures.
The UGC Publications page (ugc.ac.lk index.php?...id=102) timed out (300 s) and was not read.

No official source found giving national employment rates for Medicine, Dental Surgery or Veterinary Science graduates (UGC 2017 excluded them; MoHE 2023 has Medicine from University of Colombo only, Dentistry/Veterinary not reported).
No official national time-to-first-job or public/private split by field after 2017.
No DCS Labour Force Survey table with a separate unemployment rate for degree holders (only 'G.C.E. (A/L) & above').
